classification.difficultyReason: Set up the annuity formula, rearrange to an exponential inequality, solve with logarithms, and round up to a whole period. The same method is used in both parts.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Hamid deposits $\$2000$ at the end of each year into a superannuation fund earning 5% p.a., compounded annually. After how many years will the balance first exceed $\$50\,000$?

answer.worked:
After $n$ years the balance is a geometric series with $a=2000$, $r=1.05$:
$$2000+2000(1.05)+\cdots+2000(1.05)^{n-1}=\frac{2000\left(1.05^n-1\right)}{0.05}.$$
Solve for the balance to exceed $\$50\,000$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2000\left(1.05^n-1\right)}{0.05}&>50000\\1.05^n-1&>1.25\\1.05^n&>2.25\\n\log1.05&>\log2.25\\n&>16.62\ldots\end{align*}$$
The balance first exceeds $\$50\,000$ after 17 years.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Jess deposits $\$300$ at the end of each month into an account earning 6% p.a., compounded monthly. After how many months will the balance first exceed $\$20\,000$?

answer.worked:
Monthly growth factor $r=1+\dfrac{0.06}{12}=1.005$.
$$300+300(1.005)+\cdots+300(1.005)^{n-1}=\frac{300\left(1.005^n-1\right)}{0.005}.$$
Solve for the balance to exceed $\$20\,000$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{300\left(1.005^n-1\right)}{0.005}&>20000\\1.005^n-1&>\frac13\\1.005^n&>\frac43\\n\log1.005&>\log\frac43\\n&>57.68\ldots\end{align*}$$
The balance first exceeds $\$20\,000$ after 58 months.
